per.num_sequence_extensions: In ASN.1 PER, this indicates the number of extension fields that are present in an extensible SEQUENCE structure.
per.choice_index: In ASN.1 PER, this is the index identifying the selected option from the root set of alternatives in a CHOICE data structure.
per.choice_extension_index: In ASN.1 PER, this is the index identifying the selected option from the extension set of alternatives in a CHOICE data structure.
per.enum_index: In ASN.1 PER, this is the index identifying the selected value from the root set of an ENUMERATED type.
per.enum_extension_index: In ASN.1 PER, this is the index identifying the selected value from the extension set of an ENUMERATED type.
per.generalstring_length: The length, in characters, of a GeneralString data type in an ASN.1 message.
per.extension_bit: A single bit in ASN.1 PER that indicates whether an extensible data type, such as a SEQUENCE or CHOICE, contains extension fields.
per.extension_present_bit: A bit in ASN.1 PER indicating if an optional extension group is present in the encoded message.
per.small_number_bit: A bit used in a specific ASN.1 PER encoding scheme for non-negative integers to indicate if the number is 'small' and can be encoded in fewer bits.
per.optional_field_bit: A bit in ASN.1 PER that signals the presence or absence of an optional field within a SEQUENCE.
per.sequence_of_length: The number of elements contained within a SEQUENCE OF construct in an ASN.1 message.
per.object_length: The length in bytes of an encoded Object Identifier (OID) in an ASN.1 message.
per.open_type_length: The length in bytes of an ASN.1 Open Type field, which is a placeholder that can contain any ASN.1 type.
per.real_length: The length in bytes of an encoded REAL (floating-point) number in an ASN.1 message.
per.octet_string_length: The length in bytes of an OCTET STRING data type.
per.bit_string_length: The length in bits of a BIT STRING data type.
per.normally_small_nonnegative_whole_num: The number of bytes used to encode a non-negative integer that is expected to be small, as per ASN.1 PER rules.
per.const_int_len: The number of bytes used to encode a constrained integer, where the range of possible values is known from the schema.
per.direct_reference: An Object Identifier (OID) that directly identifies the abstract syntax of an ASN.1 EXTERNAL type.
per.indirect_reference: An integer that indirectly identifies the abstract syntax of an ASN.1 EXTERNAL type, referencing a context-specific agreement.
per.data_value_descriptor: An Object Processed Descriptor that describes the data value of an ASN.1 EXTERNAL type.
per.encoding: Specifies the encoding of an ASN.1 EXTERNAL type, such as single-ASN1-type, octet-aligned, or arbitrary.
per.single_ASN1_type: Indicates that the encoding of an ASN.1 EXTERNAL type is a single, complete ASN.1 type.
per.octet_aligned: Indicates that the encoding of an ASN.1 EXTERNAL type is a sequence of octets.
per.arbitrary: Indicates that the encoding of an ASN.1 EXTERNAL type is a sequence of bits.
per.integer_length: The number of bytes used to encode an integer value.
T_UINT3: An internal Wireshark type representing a 3-bit unsigned integer, used for ASN.1 dissection.
T_UINT6: An internal Wireshark type representing a 6-bit unsigned integer, used for ASN.1 dissection.
per.internal.num_bits: An internal Wireshark field showing the number of bits used to encode a specific PER field, for debugging purposes.
per.internal.min: An internal Wireshark field showing the minimum value for a constrained integer in PER, for debugging purposes.
per.internal.value: An internal Wireshark field showing the raw bit value of a PER field, for debugging purposes.
per.internal.min_int: An internal Wireshark field showing the minimum value for a constrained integer in PER, for debugging purposes.
per.internal.value_int: An internal Wireshark field showing the decoded integer value of a PER field, for debugging purposes.
per.encoding_boiler_plate: An informational message in Wireshark advising the user to enable PER protocol preferences to view internal decoding fields.
T_STRIN: An internal Wireshark type representing a string, used for ASN.1 dissection.
mac-nr.radio-type: Specifies the radio access technology, which in this context is NR (New Radio).
mac-nr.direction: Indicates the direction of the MAC PDU, either Uplink (from UE to gNB) or Downlink (from gNB to UE).
mac-nr.rnti: Radio Network Temporary Identifier, a 16-bit identifier used to address a UE on common physical channels.
mac-nr.rnti-type: Specifies the purpose of the RNTI, such as C-RNTI for a connected UE or RA-RNTI for random access.
mac-nr.ueid: A unique identifier for the User Equipment within the cell, typically the C-RNTI.
mac-nr.sfn: System Frame Number, a 10-bit counter (0-1023) for the 10ms radio frames, used for synchronization.
mac-nr.slot: The slot number within a 10ms radio frame, with the number of slots per frame depending on the subcarrier spacing.
mac-nr.harqid: Hybrid ARQ Process ID, used to manage multiple parallel stop-and-wait retransmission processes.
mac-nr.bcch-transport-channel: Indicates the transport channel (e.g., BCH or DL-SCH) that carried the Broadcast Control Channel (BCCH) data.
mac-nr.type2-other-cell: A Power Headroom Report (PHR) for a secondary cell in a different MAC entity, used in dual connectivity.
mac-nr.subheader: A header for a MAC Service Data Unit (SDU) or a MAC Control Element (CE) within a MAC PDU.
mac-nr.subheader.reserved: A reserved bit in the MAC subheader, set to zero and ignored by the receiver.
mac-nr.subheader.f: A format bit in the MAC subheader indicating if the length field is 1 byte (F=0) or 2 bytes (F=1).
mac-nr.subheader.sdu-length: The length in bytes of the associated MAC Service Data Unit (SDU).
mac-nr.lcid: Logical Channel ID, a 6-bit value in the MAC subheader that identifies the type of data or the specific logical channel.
mac-nr.ulsch.lcid: The Logical Channel ID for data multiplexed onto the Uplink Shared Channel (UL-SCH).
mac-nr.dlsch.lcid: The Logical Channel ID for data multiplexed onto the Downlink Shared Channel (DL-SCH).
mac-nr.dlsch.elcid-2oct: A 2-octet extended Logical Channel ID (eLCID) used for specific MAC Control Elements in NR-U (NR in Unlicensed spectrum).
mac-nr.dlsch.elcid-1oct: A 1-octet extended Logical Channel ID (eLCID) used for specific MAC Control Elements in NR-U (NR in Unlicensed spectrum).
mac-nr.ulsch.sdu: The MAC Service Data Unit (payload) carried on the Uplink Shared Channel.
mac-nr.dlsch.sdu: The MAC Service Data Unit (payload) carried on the Downlink Shared Channel.
mac-nr.bcch.pdu: The Protocol Data Unit for the Broadcast Control Channel, typically containing a MIB or SIB1.
mac-nr.pcch.pdu: The Protocol Data Unit for the Paging Control Channel, containing the Paging message.
mac-nr.rar: Random Access Response (RAR), the MAC PDU sent by the gNB as Msg2 in the random access procedure.
mac-nr.rar.e: The Extension bit in a RAR subheader, which indicates if another RAR subheader (for BI or RAPID) follows.
mac-nr.rar.t: The Type bit in a RAR subheader, which indicates if the payload contains a Backoff Indicator (T=0) or a RAPID (T=1).
mac-nr.rar.reserved: A reserved bit in the Random Access Response payload.
mac-nr.rar.subheader: The subheader for a Random Access Response within the MAC PDU.
mac-nr.rar.bi: Backoff Indicator, a value in the RAR that instructs the UE how long to wait before retrying random access.
mac-nr.rar.rapid: Random Access Preamble ID, an echo of the preamble sent by the UE, allowing it to identify its specific RAR.
mac-nr.rar.ta: Timing Advance command in the RAR, used to adjust the UE's uplink transmission timing for Msg3.
mac-nr.rar.grant: The uplink grant provided in the RAR, specifying resources for the UE to transmit Msg3.
mac-nr.rar.grant.hopping: A flag indicating whether frequency hopping is enabled for the Msg3 PUSCH transmission.
mac-nr.rar.grant.fra: Frequency Resource Allocation for the Msg3 PUSCH transmission.
mac-nr.rar.grant.tsa: Time Resource Allocation for the Msg3 PUSCH transmission.
mac-nr.rar.grant.mcs: Modulation and Coding Scheme to be used for the Msg3 PUSCH transmission.
mac-nr.rar.grant.tcsp: Transmit Power Control (TPC) command for the Msg3 PUSCH transmission.
mac-nr.rar.grant.csi: Channel State Information (CSI) request, a flag indicating if the UE should include a CSI report in Msg3.
mac-nr.rar.temp_crnti: Temporary Cell RNTI assigned to the UE in the RAR, used for subsequent communication until contention resolution.
mac-nr.msgb: Message B, the response message from the gNB in the 2-step random access procedure.
mac-nr.msgb.subheader: The subheader for a Message B payload within a MAC PDU.
mac-nr.msgb.e: Extension bit in the Message B subheader.
mac-nr.msgb.t1: Type 1 bit in the Message B subheader.
mac-nr.msgb.t2: Type 2 bit in the Message B subheader.
mac-nr.msgb.s: MAC SDU indicator bit in the Message B subheader.
mac-nr.msgb.reserved: A reserved field in the Message B payload.
mac-nr.msgb.ta-command: Timing Advance Command included in Message B.
mac-nr.msgb.channelaccess-cpext: Channel Access CP extension field in Message B, relevant for NR-U.
mac-nr.msgb.tpc: Transmit Power Control (TPC) command for the PUCCH resource carrying HARQ feedback for Message B.
mac-nr.msgb.harq-feedback-timing-indicat: Indicates the PDSCH-to-HARQ_feedback timing for the Message B PDSCH.
mac-nr.msgb.pucch-resource-indicator: Indicates the PUCCH resource for the UE to send HARQ feedback for Message B.

nas_5gs.mm.ctrl_plane_serv_type: Indicates the type of service requested by the UE via the control plane, such as mobile-originated data, signalling, or emergency services.

nas_5gs.mm.nas_sec_algo_ip: Specifies the integrity protection algorithm (e.g., NIA1, NIA2) selected by the network to prevent tampering of NAS messages.
nas_5gs.mm.s1_mode_b0: A capability bit indicating the UE supports interworking with the 4G Evolved Packet Core (EPC) via the S1 interface, also known as N26 interface support.
nas_5gs.mm.ho_attach_b1: A capability bit indicating the UE supports performing an Attach procedure that includes a request for PDU session establishment, typically for handover from a non-3GPP access.
nas_5gs.mm.lpp_cap_b2: A capability bit indicating the UE supports the LTE Positioning Protocol (LPP) for location services.
nas_5gs.mm.restrict_ec_b3: A capability bit indicating the UE is subject to network-imposed restrictions on the use of Enhanced Coverage (EC) features.
nas_5gs.mm.5g_cp_ciot_b4: A capability bit indicating the UE supports Control Plane CIoT 5GS optimization, allowing small data transfer over NAS signalling without establishing a user plane connection.
nas_5gs.mm.n3_data_b5: A capability bit indicating the UE supports transferring user plane data over the N3 interface for a PDU session that was established with a 'control plane only' indication.
nas_5gs.mm.5g_iphc_cp_ciot_b6: A capability bit indicating the UE supports IP header compression (using ROHC) for data transferred via the Control Plane CIoT 5GS optimization.
nas_5gs.mm.sgc_b7: A capability bit indicating the UE supports Service Gap Control (SGC), a power-saving feature that allows the network to configure time intervals during which the UE is not reachable.
nas_5gs.mm.5g_srvcc_b0: A capability bit indicating the UE supports Single Radio Voice Call Continuity (SRVCC) for voice calls from 5G NG-RAN to 3G UTRAN.
nas_5gs.mm.5g_up_ciot_b1: A capability bit indicating the UE supports User Plane CIoT 5GS optimization, which includes features like suspending and resuming RRC connections efficiently for sporadic data.
nas_5gs.mm.v2x_b2: A capability bit indicating the UE supports Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) services over the 5G network.
nas_5gs.mm.v2xcepc5_b3: A capability bit indicating the UE supports V2X communication directly with other UEs over the E-UTRA (LTE) PC5 interface.
nas_5gs.mm.v2xcnpc5_b4: A capability bit indicating the UE supports V2X communication directly with other UEs over the NR PC5 interface.
nas_5gs.mm.5g_lcs_b5: A capability bit indicating the UE supports 5G Location Services (LCS) notification mechanisms, such as receiving notifications about privacy requirements.
nas_5gs.mm.nssaa_b6: A capability bit indicating the UE supports performing a separate authentication and authorization procedure for a specific network slice.
nas_5gs.mm.racs_b7: A capability bit indicating the UE supports Radio Capability Signalling (RACS) optimization, which allows the network to manage and retrieve UE radio capabilities more efficiently.
nas_5gs.mm.cag_b0: A capability bit indicating the UE supports Closed Access Group (CAG) functionality, allowing it to access cells that are restricted to a specific group of subscribers.
nas_5gs.mm.wsusa_b1: A capability bit indicating the UE can receive and use Wake-Up Signal (WUS) assistance information from the network to reduce power consumption.
nas_5gs.mm.multiple_up_b2: A capability bit indicating the UE supports establishing multiple user-plane paths for a single PDU session, used for features like ATSSS.
nas_5gs.mm.ehc_cp_ciot_b3: A capability bit indicating the UE supports Ethernet header compression for data transferred via the Control Plane CIoT 5GS optimization.
nas_5gs.mm.er_nssai_b4: A capability bit indicating the UE supports receiving an extended format of the Rejected NSSAI, which can include a back-off timer for each rejected S-NSSAI.
nas_5gs.mm.prose_dd_b5: A capability bit indicating the UE supports 5G Proximity-based Services (ProSe) for direct discovery of other UEs without network involvement.
nas_5gs.mm.prose_dc_b6: A capability bit indicating the UE supports 5G Proximity-based Services (ProSe) for direct communication with other UEs over the PC5 interface.
nas_5gs.mm.prose_l2relay_b7: A capability bit indicating the UE can act as a Layer-2 relay for 5G Proximity-based Services (ProSe), extending network coverage for remote UEs.

nas_5gs.sup_andsp: An indication of whether the UE supports Access Network Discovery and Selection Policy (ANDSP).
nas_5gs.nssui: An indication from the UE on how it handles URSP rules for non-subscribed Stand-Alone Non-Public Networks (SNPNs).
nas_5gs.upsi_sublist_len: The length of a UE Policy Section Identifier (UPSI) sublist.
nas_5gs.upsc: The UE Policy Section Counter (UPSC), used to track updates to UE policy sections.
nas_5gs.os_id: The Operating System ID (a UUID) of the UE, used for policy matching.
nas_5gs.os_id_len: The length of the OS ID.
nas_5gs.upds_cause: The cause for a UE Policy Delivery Service (UPDS) procedure failure.
nas_5gs.v2xuui: An indicator from the UE that it requests UE policies for V2X communication over the Uu interface.
nas_5gs.v2xpc5i: An indicator from the UE that it requests UE policies for V2X communication over the PC5 interface.
nas_5gs.app_id_len: The length of an OS-specific Application ID.
nas_5gs.os_app_id: An OS-specific Application ID, used for policy matching.
nas_5gs.mm.len_of_rej_s_nssai: The length of a rejected S-NSSAI information element.
nas_5gs.mm.rej_s_nssai.cause: The cause value indicating why a specific S-NSSAI was rejected by the network.
nas_5gs.mm.ue_radio_cap_id: An identifier assigned by the network to the UE's radio capability information, which can be used for efficient retrieval in the future (RACS).
nas_5gs.mm.ue_radio_cap_id_del_req: A request from the UE to delete its stored UE radio capability ID from the network.
nas_5gs.mm.trunc_amf_set_id: A truncated version of the AMF Set ID.
nas_5gs.mm.trunc_amf_pointer: A truncated version of the AMF Pointer.
nas_5gs.mm.n5gcreg: An indication from a dual-mode NB-IoT/NR device that it is capable of 5GC registration.
nas_5gs.mm.nb_n1_drx_value: The DRX value for NB-IoT connected to 5GC (NB-N1 mode).
nas_5gs.mm.scmr: An indication from the UE that it wishes to maintain the NAS signalling connection for an extended period.
nas_5gs.mm.extended_rejected_s_nssai.num: The number of elements in the extended rejected S-NSSAI list.
nas_5gs.mm.extended_rejected_s_nssai.typ: The type of list for the extended rejected S-NSSAI.
nas_5gs.mm.extended_rejected_s_nssai.spa: Spare bits reserved for future use.
nas_5gs.mm.extended_rejected_s_nssai.bac: A back-off timer value associated with a rejected S-NSSAI, indicating how long the UE must wait before retrying.
nas_5gs.mm.rejected_s_nssai.length: The length of a rejected S-NSSAI information element.
nas_5gs.mm.rejected_s_nssai.cause_value: The cause value indicating why a specific S-NSSAI was rejected by the network.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.type: The type of paging restriction being applied, such as restricting paging for all non-GBR QoS flows.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_7: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 7.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_6: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 6.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_5: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 5.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_4: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 4.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_3: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 3.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_2: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 2.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_1: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 1.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_0: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 0.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_15: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 15.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_14: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 14.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_13: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 13.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_12: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 12.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_11: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 11.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_10: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 10.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_9: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 9.
nas_5gs.mm.paging_restriction.psi_8: A bit in a bitmap indicating if paging is restricted for the PDU session with ID 8.
nas_5gs.mm.nid.assign_mode: Specifies whether the Network Identifier (NID) for a Non-Public Network (NPN) is assigned by the network or is self-assigned by the UE.
nas_5gs.mm.nid.value: The actual value of the Network Identifier (NID), which, combined with a PLMN ID, uniquely identifies a Stand-alone Non-Public Network (SNPN).
nas_5gs.mm.eips_assist_info.type: Indicates the type of assistance information provided by the network to the UE for Enhanced Idle mode Paging for Satellite access (EIPS), such as paging subgrouping or paging probability.
nas_5gs.mm.eips_assist_info.paging_subgr: Identifies the specific subgroup a UE belongs to for paging, allowing the UE to monitor for pages only during its subgroup's specific time slots to save power in satellite networks.
nas_5gs.mm.eips_assist_info.ue_paging_pr: Provides the UE with the probability of being paged, enabling it to make power-saving decisions, such as entering a deep sleep state if the probability is low.
nas_5gs.mm.add_request_result.prd: Indicates the network's decision on whether to apply paging restrictions for the UE, which can limit paging attempts in certain tracking areas to reduce signaling load.
nas_5gs.mm.nssrg_info.len: Specifies the length of the Network Slice-Specific Re-authentication and Re-keying Group (NSSRG) values associated with a particular S-NSSAI.
nas_5gs.mm.nssrg_info.s_nssai_len: Indicates the length of the S-NSSAI (Single Network Slice Selection Assistance Information) that is associated with the provided NSSRG information.
nas_5gs.mm.nssrg_info.nssrg: The value of the Network Slice-Specific Re-authentication and Re-keying Group (NSSRG), which groups UEs for collective security procedures within a specific network slice.
nas_5gs.mm.nsag_info.len: Specifies the total length of the Network Slice Admission and Congestion control Group (NSAG) information element.
nas_5gs.mm.nsag_info.identifier: A unique identifier for a Network Slice Admission and Congestion control Group (NSAG), used to apply common admission and congestion control policies to a group of UEs.
nas_5gs.mm.nsag_info.s_nssai_len: Indicates the length of the list of S-NSSAIs that are members of this specific Network Slice Admission and Congestion control Group (NSAG).
nas_5gs.mm.nsag_info.priority: Defines the priority level of the NSAG, which the network can use to make admission or congestion control decisions, prioritizing traffic from higher-priority groups.
nas_5gs.mm.nsag_info.tais_list_len: Specifies the length of the list of Tracking Area Identities (TAIs) where the policies associated with this NSAG are valid.
nas_5gs.mm.prose_relay_trans_id: A transaction identifier used to correlate request and response messages for a specific Proximity-based Services (ProSe) relay operation, such as a key request.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_req_params.relay_se: A code that identifies the specific ProSe Layer-3 UE-to-Network relay service being requested, allowing the network to authorize the service and derive appropriate security keys.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_req_params.nonce_1: A random number generated by the initiator of a relay key request to prevent replay attacks and ensure the freshness of the subsequent key derivation process.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_req_params.ruit: Indicates the type of identity (e.g., 5G-S-TMSI) being used for the remote UE in a ProSe UE-to-Network relay scenario.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_req_params.remote_u: The actual identifier of the remote UE that is requesting network access via the ProSe relay UE.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_resp_params.5gpii: An indication (5GPRUK ID indication) of whether a new 5G ProSe Relay User Key (5GPRUK) Identifier is being provided by the network in the response.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_resp_params.key_knr: The UE-to-Network Relay Key (KNR_ProSe) provided by the network to the relay UE to secure the communication link with the remote UE.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_resp_params.nonce_2: A random number generated by the network in response to a relay key request, used in conjunction with Nonce_1 to ensure freshness and prevent replay attacks.
nas_5gs.mm.relay_key_resp_params.5gpruk_: The identifier for the 5G ProSe Relay User Key (5GPRUK), a long-term key from which short-term relay session keys are derived.
nas_5gs.mm.priority_indicator.mpsi: The Multimedia Priority Service (MPSI) indicator, which, when set, signals that the UE is requesting prioritized handling for its session, typically for critical communications.
